title: Back and Forward remember searches: Back from a folder opened out of the results returns to the results, and Back during a search only ends the search
problem: A search is not part of a window's history. `Location` only has Folder/Recents/Results/Trash (src/model.rs:8-21) and `History` stores bare `Location`s (src/model.rs:118-165). Every way out of a search clears it first: `navigate` calls `end_search` before `history.navigate` (src/finder/mod.rs:893-898), as do `go_up` (975-988) and `reveal_in_place` (1005-1011); `end_search` empties the field and the query (1350-1356). So double-clicking a folder in the results (`open_entries` -> `navigate`, mod.rs:2019-2023), or using Show in Enclosing Folder, and then pressing Back lands on the plain folder the search started from: the words, the scope and Name/Contents are gone and have to be typed again. `go_back` also ends the search and pops a folder in the same press (960-966), so searching in B after coming from A and pressing Back puts you in A, not B's listing; `go_forward` (968-973) can never bring a search back. Results sent by `fff show` do survive Back/Forward because they are a `Location` (tests/finder.rs:294-299), so typed searches are the odd one out. Finder and Explorer both return to the results, then to the folder.
proposal: Make a search a step in the history. src/model.rs: add `pub struct SavedSearch { pub query: String, pub in_folder: bool, pub contents: bool }` and make the back/forward stacks hold `Visit { location: Location, search: Option<SavedSearch> }` (`follow` keeps mapping the locations). `navigate(to, live: Option<SavedSearch>)`: when `live` is Some push `Visit{current, None}` and then `Visit{current, live}`, so Back returns first to the results and then to the plain folder, and an entry is pushed even when `to` equals the current folder (reveal_in_place into the same folder); otherwise push the current visit as today. `back(live)`: when `live` is Some, push `Visit{current, live}` on `forward` and stay on the same location (the search just ends); otherwise pop as today and return the popped visit's `search`. `forward(live)` mirrors it. src/finder/mod.rs: add `live_search()` (Some while `is_searching()`, from `query`, `scope`, `search_contents`) and `restore_search(Option<SavedSearch>, window, cx)` (set `self.scope` and `self.search_contents`, `search_input.set_value(..)`, `set_query(query, true, cx)`, the same steps `open_request` uses at mod.rs:819-824; None -> `end_search`). Take the snapshot before `end_search` in `navigate`, `go_up`, `reveal_in_place`, `go_back` and `go_forward`; in `go_back`/`go_forward` call `location_changed` only when the location really changed, then `restore_search`. Make the toolbar's Back button enabled while searching (src/finder/toolbar.rs:310 uses `history.can_back()` only). The Kind filter stays out of the snapshot; it is already a saved per-tab setting. Update docs/manual.md (the Toolbar table's Back/Forward row and the Searching section) and CHANGELOG.md.
original_test_plan: Unit tests in src/model.rs beside `history_back_forward`: navigate with a live search then back() twice yields (A, Some(search)) then (A, None); forward() twice returns to the search and then the folder; back(live) keeps the location and makes forward restore the search; a saved search survives `follow`. Headless test in tests/finder.rs: open the fixture, Cmd+F, type `atlas`, double-click the `atlas` folder result (`f.click_row(ix, Default::default(), 2, window, cx)`), assert folder == Projects/atlas and `!is_searching()`; press Cmd+[ and assert `query() == "atlas"`, `scope-computer` exists, folder == fixture root and the names contain `Project Atlas.txt`; press Cmd+[ again and assert the query is empty and `ui.folder()` is the fixture folder (not its parent) with its four items; press Cmd+] and assert the search is back; press Cmd+] again and assert Projects/atlas with no search.
original_risks: Every direct `self.history.navigate/back/forward` caller must pass the live search (go_up, reveal_in_place, open_smart_folder, open_request). `History::follow` (moved folders) must keep working on Visits. Existing tests assert Back from Results/Recents goes to the folder and that Back selects the folder just left (go_back passes `from`); those paths must stay unchanged when no search is live. A restored search runs again, so rows and selection can differ from what was left; `location_changed` reloads the listing under the restored search (harmless: results overlay it). Smart Folders and `Location::Results` must keep working. Each tab and split pane has its own History; a tab moved to a new window still loses it, as today. Reviewers differed on two points: one included Kind in the snapshot (two left it out), and one made 'Back only ends the search' an optional second step (two made it core). The history-menus candidate builds on the same History type.

verifier.claim_check:
The described behaviour is true and nothing already handles it.
- src/model.rs:8-21 `Location` is Folder/Recents/Results/Trash; `History` (118-165) keeps `back: Vec<Location>`, `forward: Vec<Location>`, `current: Location`. No search state.
- src/finder/mod.rs:893-898 `navigate` calls `end_search` then `history.navigate`; `go_up` (975-988) and `reveal_in_place` (1005-1011) do the same; `end_search` (1350-1356) empties the field and query.
- `go_back` (960-966) calls `end_search` and `history.back()` in one press; `go_forward` (968-973) likewise. A search can never come back.
- `open_entries` (2013-2023) sends a folder result through `navigate`; Show in Enclosing Folder (src/finder/menus.rs:200-205) uses `reveal_in_place`.
- Toolbar: src/finder/toolbar.rs:310 uses `history.can_back()` only, so Back is disabled in a fresh window even while searching.
- Other ways out of a search (Escape at mod.rs:1962-1973, the field's clear button, `new_folder` at 2778) end it with no history; the proposal leaves those alone.
- Docs: docs/manual.md:179 says only "Move through the window's history"; the Searching section (322-338) and CHANGELOG.md say nothing about Back and searches. The behaviour is undocumented, not intentional.
- Tests: no test presses Back/Forward with a live search. Back is pressed in tests/finder.rs:25-36 and 294, tests/controls.rs:43-58, tests/basics.rs:240-247, tests/folder_tree.rs:92 and 284, tests/settings.rs:232, all with no search live. tests/finder.rs:303-314 calls `open_request` (reveal_in_place) with a live search but only asserts folder and selection, which still hold.

Where the proposal is wrong: its History mechanics give dead presses. `navigate` pushes two entries, (A, None) then (A, search), and `back(live)` ends the search without popping. Trace: open a folder from results in A; Back restores the search; Back ends it and leaves (A, None) on the back stack; the next Back pops (A, None) and nothing visible changes. Going Forward again pushes another (A, None), so they pile up. "`forward(live)` mirrors it" is also wrong: Forward during a live search must not just end it. The proposed headless test presses Back only twice at the fixture root, so it would not catch this.
verifier.implementation_notes:
Keep the goal; replace the History mechanics with a single push and a "redo" rule on Forward.

**src/model.rs**
- Add `#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct SavedSearch { pub query: String, pub in_folder: bool, pub contents: bool }`. Use a bool, not `SearchScope`, which lives in src/finder/mod.rs:77 and model.rs is GPUI-free.
- Add private `struct Visit { location: Location, search: Option<SavedSearch> }`. Stacks become `Vec<Visit>`; `current` stays a `Location`, so `current()`, `follow`'s return value and every `history.current()` caller are untouched.
- Add `pub struct Step { pub moved: bool, pub search: Option<SavedSearch> }`.
- `navigate(&mut self, to, live: Option<SavedSearch>) -> bool` returns whether the location changed.
  - `to == current` and `live` is None: return false, as today.
  - `to == current` and `live` is Some: push `Visit{current.clone(), live}` on back, clear forward, return false. This covers reveal_in_place into the searched folder.
  - Otherwise: push `Visit{old current, live}` (one entry), clear forward, return true.
- `back(&mut self, live) -> Option<Step>`:
  - `live` is Some: push `Visit{current.clone(), live}` on forward, do not pop, return `Step{moved: false, search: None}`.
  - Otherwise pop `prev`, push `Visit{current, None}` on forward, set current, return `Step{moved: prev.location != old, search: prev.search}`.
- `forward(&mut self, live) -> Option<Step>`: pop `next`.
  - `next.location == current`, `live` is None and `next.search` is Some: this is the search Back ended. Push nothing, return `Step{moved: false, search: next.search}`.
  - Otherwise push `Visit{current, live}` on back, set current, return `Step{moved, search: next.search}`.
- In both `back` and `forward`, skip a popped visit that equals the present state (same location, no search, no live search). This guards the rare same-folder-reveal, Back, Escape, Forward sequence.
- `follow` iterates `visit.location`. `can_back`/`can_forward` are unchanged.
- Resulting sequence for X -> A -> search -> open T: Back gives A with results, Back gives plain A, Back gives X; Forward retraces all three. No dead presses.

**src/finder/mod.rs**
- `fn live_search(&self) -> Option<SavedSearch>` from `is_searching()`, `query`, `scope == SearchScope::Folder`, `search_contents`.
- `fn restore_search(&mut self, s: SavedSearch, window, cx)`: assign `self.scope` and `self.search_contents` directly, before the query; then `search_input.set_value` and `set_query(q, true, cx)` as `open_request` does at 819-824; then `cx.notify()` so the toolbar scope button redraws.
- `navigate`, `go_up`: take `live_search()` before `end_search`, pass it to `history.navigate`, call `location_changed` only when it returns true.
- `reveal_in_place`: same, but keep calling `location_changed(Some(item))` always, as today.
- `go_back`: take `from` and `live` first, then `end_search`, then `history.back(live)`. Call `location_changed(from)` if `step.moved`, then `restore_search` if `step.search` is Some. `go_forward` is the same with `None` for the selection.
- `end_search` must run before `restore_search`: `set_query` returns early when the query is unchanged (1325).
- `can_go_back()` (747) and src/finder/toolbar.rs:310 become `history.can_back() || is_searching()`.
- Leave `open_smart_folder` (src/finder/filter.rs:215-237) alone: its scoped branch goes through `navigate` and saves the old search for free; the unscoped branch keeps replacing the search.
- All other callers use `Finder::navigate` (sidebar, path bar, dialogs, trash, volumes, transfer, folder_tree), so they need no edits.

**Pitfalls**
- Selection after Back into results is racy. `location_changed(from)` selects `from` when the listing arrives (1091-1102), which only works if the search results arrived first. Either do not assert it, or add a `select_in_results: Option<PathBuf>` consumed in `run_search`'s completion after `rebuild_rows` (around 1428-1431) and cleared in `set_query`.
- `set_query` resets `result_sort` to Relevance when a search starts (1340-1346), so a restored search loses a chosen result sort unless `SavedSearch` carries it. Optional.
- The search field's input events are harmless: `on_search_event` reads the field's current value (1305) and `set_query` no-ops on an equal query.
- Cmd+[ works with the search field focused: gpui-base's Input binds cmd-[/ctrl-[ to Outdent but propagates for single-line inputs (gpui-base-0.8.1/src/input/editor/indent.rs:257-259). Alt+Left in the field stays word movement.

**Docs**: docs/manual.md:179 (Back, Forward row) and the Searching section near 324-326; CHANGELOG.md under [Unreleased] > Changed.
verifier.test_plan:
All cross-platform; runs headless on Linux.

**Unit tests, src/model.rs** (beside `history_back_forward`; existing calls there and in `history_follows_folders_that_moved` gain a `None` argument):
- navigate(B, Some(s)) from A, then back(None) gives A with Some(s); back(Some(s)) keeps A, moved false, search None; back(None) goes to the entry before A. No press leaves the state unchanged.
- forward(None) three times retraces: plain A, then A with s (moved false), then B when called with live Some(s).
- navigate(current, Some(s)) pushes an entry and returns false; navigate(current, None) is still a no-op.
- A saved search survives `follow`: the visit's folder moves and the search is kept.
- A popped visit equal to the present state is skipped.

**Headless test, tests/finder.rs** (new `#[gpui_kit::test]`, using `Fixture::new`, `Ui::open`, `ui.go_to`, `ui.press(&cmd("f"))`, `ui.type_text`, `ui.names()`, `ui.update(|f, window, cx| f.click_row(ix, Default::default(), 2, window, cx))`, `ui.folder()`, `ui.exists("scope-computer")`, `ui.read(|f| f.query().to_string())`, `ui.read(|f| f.is_searching())`):
1. `ui.go_to(&fx.path("Projects"))` so there is a folder behind the search.
2. Cmd+F, type `atlas`; find `ix` with `ui.names().iter().position(|n| n == "atlas")`; double-click it. Assert folder is Projects/atlas and not searching.
3. Cmd+[: query is "atlas", folder is Projects, names contain "Project Atlas.txt", `scope-computer` exists.
4. Cmd+[: query empty, folder still Projects, names are ["atlas"].
5. Cmd+[: folder is the fixture root. This is the dead-press check.
6. Cmd+] three times: Projects with no search; Projects with query "atlas"; Projects/atlas with no search.
7. Scope and Name/Contents: before leaving a search, `ui.click("scope-folder")` and `ui.click("by-contents")`; navigate away with `ui.go_to`; Cmd+[; assert `search_scope() == SearchScope::Folder` and `searches_contents()`.
8. Same-folder reveal: search, then `ui.update(|f, w, cx| f.reveal_in_place(&fx.path("Roadmap.md"), w, cx))`, then Cmd+[ and assert the query is back.

**Toolbar test, tests/controls.rs** (beside `back_and_forward_buttons`): in a fresh window, `ui.update(|f, _, cx| f.set_query("atlas".into(), true, cx))`, `ui.click("back")`, assert not searching and the folder unchanged; `ui.click("forward")`, assert query is "atlas". The harness cannot read a button's disabled state, so the click having an effect is the check.

Existing tests that must stay green unchanged: tests/finder.rs `lists_navigates_and_goes_back` and `results_sent_from_nushell`, tests/controls.rs `back_and_forward_buttons` and `search_scope_button`, tests/basics.rs `the_mouse_back_and_forward_buttons_navigate`, tests/folder_tree.rs:92 and 284, tests/settings.rs:232.
verifier.risks:
- Behaviour change beyond the headline case: any navigation away from a live search (sidebar, path bar, Go to Folder, Cmd+Up) now saves it, so getting back to the folder before the search takes one more Back press. Back during a search no longer leaves the folder. Both match Finder and Explorer but need a CHANGELOG "Changed" entry.
- The proposal as written would ship dead Back/Forward presses; the single-push model above avoids them. The unit tests must assert that no press leaves the state unchanged.
- A restored search runs again: rows can differ, scroll position and result sort are not restored, and a Contents search costs its full time again.
- Selecting the folder just left inside restored results depends on whether the listing or the search finishes first, unless a pending-select field is added.
- Restoring sets `self.scope`, which also flips the sticky "Search Only in This Folder" toolbar button.
- Kind and the Nushell filter stay outside the snapshot, so a restored search uses whatever they are now.
- Searches ended by Escape or the clear button are not recorded, so Forward will not bring those back. This is consistent but should be stated in the manual.
- This touches the core navigation type; the history-menus candidate builds on `History` and should land after it or be coordinated with it.
